issues.description: The problem specification (UML and task text) and the template Farm.java define singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) as void methods that print the song (i.e., they are expected to perform printing). However, the solution implementation changes both methods to return String (singFarmSong() returns String and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) returns String) and does not perform the printing inside singFarmSong(). This return-type/behavior mismatch between the solution and the problem/template will confuse students about whether they should print the song or return it as a String, and may cause tests or student code that follow the template/UML to fail when compared to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification and template: change singFarmSong() to have a void return type and perform the printing (System.out.println) directly, and change singFarmSongVerse(Animal) to void and print the verse lines rather than returning a String. Alternatively, if returning the song is intentional, update the UML, problem text, and template method signatures to indicate singFarmSong():String and singFarmSongVerse(Animal):String and clarify that the caller is responsible for printing.
